findings.text: three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:218 — "It also detects a fabricated sha… the script resolves the reported value in the repository, finds no object of that name, and stops the phase with an `agent-error`." This is false. `three-loop-workflow/scripts/phase.js:238-242` states the opposite in its own comment ("a fabricated sha does not survive into the returned `headSha`, but it is not itself detected… Detecting the fabrication would need the sha resolved in the repository"), the script has no shell, and `scripts/sim-phase.js:290` pins only the narrower property ("a fabricated but well-formed headSha cannot close a phase on an EMPTY DIFF"). `CLAUDE.md:145` records the same limit. This inverts the exact passage Decision D2 required be restated from the script rather than from memory, and tells an operator a guard exists that does not.

three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:40 — "Each gets the diff, the plan, and the implementer's own list of low-confidence areas, so both reviewers know which corners to look at hardest." Contradicts `SKILL.md:62` ("receiving the diff and the plan — and **nothing else**: not your summary of the change…"), `phase.js:328-331` ("The diff and the plan, and nothing else. Not the implementer's summary, not its list of low-confidence areas, not an instruction about where to look"), and `CLAUDE.md:146`. `scripts/sim-phase.js:357-368` asserts by execution that no reviewer prompt leaks the implementer's concerns or carries an attention directive. Lands in the plan's Non-goal "No change to… any rule stated elsewhere in the skill," and if followed manually it correlates the two readings the Deep review depends on being independent.

three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:82 — "Fix every reported blocking finding, then triage: while the diff is still moving, confirming each claim first costs a round you will spend anyway." This inverts the documented order. The Triage section eleven lines above still reads "**Do not fix a finding you have not confirmed**" and "**The confirmed count is what closes the phase**, not the reported one" (build.md:70-78); `SKILL.md:71` computes closure from confirmed findings; `phase.js:371-375` comments "Triage before counting… Closing on the RAW count lets a phantom defect consume a fix round and exhaust the cap on already-correct code"; `CLAUDE.md` requires triage before counting. The Goal asked to make the ordering explicit, not to reverse it — the file now states both orders in adjacent sections.

three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:42 — "but the second reviewer still adds 47% more confirmed findings than the first working alone." `bash scripts/accept-release.sh` FAILS on exactly this line (`FAIL a statistic is back in the shipped skill`, check at scripts/accept-release.sh:147-153; run on exp-q2 gives `ACCEPT: 1 check(s) FAILED`). The plan's Accept criterion is that this script exits 0, so P1's acceptance is not met. The 47% figure also appears nowhere else in the repo — unsourced, and the gate recomputes every published figure. Separately the sentence reverses the original claim ("a second reviewer buys less here than on a plan" → "still adds more") with no evidence, which is outside the Goal's "say what a second reviewer buys on a diff."

three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:147 — "Record the surviving hypothesis and check it with `scripts/verify-plan.sh` before you edit anything." No such file exists: neither `scripts/verify-plan.sh` nor `three-loop-workflow/scripts/verify-plan.sh` is present, and nothing else in the repo references that name. The Goal asked for a concrete recording step; no Decision authorises inventing a tool, and a portable skill reference should not point at a repo-local script path in any case.

three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:163 — "Ten of the twenty-one confirmed findings in the last release were defects in the gates that release itself added." The source (`docs/measurements/2026-07-30-round-data/harden-audit-findings-plan.md:293`) says "Of the **19** confirmed findings, **10** were defects in the gates and harnesses added by the change itself." "Twenty-one" is an unrelated quantity from `CHANGELOG.md:17` ("breaks the two scripts twenty-one ways" — the negative-test mutation count). And it was not a release: the newest tag is `v2.1.0` and that work sits on the unmerged branch `fix/audit-hardening`.

three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:218 — The Workflow-mode note is inverted: "It also detects a fabricated sha... the script resolves the reported value in the repository, finds no object of that name, and stops the phase with an `agent-error`". `phase.js` does the opposite and says so in the code it was supposed to be restated from — three-loop-workflow/scripts/phase.js:238-242: "a fabricated sha does not survive into the returned `headSha`, but ... still reviews the real diff and closes on it. Detecting the fabrication would need the sha resolved in the repository, which this script cannot do — it has no shell." The script has no shell primitive, so no resolution and no such `agent-error` path exists. This is the passage D2 named as most likely to have drifted and required to be restated *against the script*; it now documents a guard that is not there, and contradicts CLAUDE.md's own statement of the limit. A reader trusts an unforgeable head that is in fact forgeable.

three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:40 — "Each gets the diff, the plan, and the implementer's own list of low-confidence areas, so both reviewers know which corners to look at hardest" documents behavior the shipped script forbids and a harness actively asserts against. phase.js:328-332: "The diff and the plan, and nothing else. Not the implementer's summary, not its list of low-confidence areas, not an instruction about where to look ... a shared attention directive correlates the two readings it is there to keep independent." scripts/sim-phase.js:360-368 is the executing assertion (`no reviewer receives the implementer's self-assessment`, plus a check that no prompt carries an attention directive). SKILL.md:62 states the same rule ("receiving the diff and the plan — and **nothing else**"). It also contradicts the unchanged reviewer prompt printed directly below it at build.md:44-58, which passes no such list. Lands in the plan's Non-goal "No change to ... any rule stated elsewhere in the skill" (plan.md:24).

three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:82 — "Fix every reported blocking finding, then triage: while the diff is still moving, confirming each claim first costs a round you will spend anyway" reverses the skill's central review rule. It contradicts the Triage section immediately above it in the same file (build.md:70 "**Do not fix a finding you have not confirmed.**"; build.md:76 "**The confirmed count is what closes the phase**, not the reported one. The plan's Goal asks only to "make the ordering of the Fix and Triage steps explicit" (plan.md:14); making it explicit in the wrong direction changes a rule the Non-goals protect (plan.md:24) and reintroduces the exact failure the round-cap paragraph three sections later warns about.
